title: Halve head dim: 4 heads -> 8 heads (HEAD_DIM 128 -> 64)
description: HEAD_DIM 128 -> 64, so model_dim stays 512 but attention uses 8 heads of 64 instead of 4 heads of 128; nothing else changed.
reflection: NEGATIVE: val_bpb 0.999160 vs baseline 0.997358, worse by 0.0018. The change was parameter- and FLOP-neutral as predicted and it was even slightly FASTER (steady-state MFU 34.0% vs ~33%, 423.9M tokens vs ~412M, 3234 steps), so the model saw ~3% MORE data and still lost. That makes this a clean readout: at dim 512 the quality-per-token of 8 narrow heads is distinctly worse than 4 wide ones, and the loss is not a throughput artifact. Head width, not head count, is what this configuration wants -- plausibly because QK-norm over 64 channels is a noisier normalizer and because 64-dim rotary halves the frequency resolution. Two follow-ups are now dead, not worth a slot: HEAD_DIM 32 (further in the losing direction) and GQA (n_kv_head < n_head only shrinks head count further). The interesting open direction is the opposite one: HEAD_DIM 256 gives 2 heads at dim 512, probably too few, but it suggests head width is a live axis via ASPECT_RATIO/DEPTH rather than via the head split. Peak VRAM unchanged at 22.7 GB.
